Logo Round 2 · Converged on your picks · For Akshit

The Long Play

The signature, cream on green, as the hero. Now we settle the small questions.
Register Signature — fine ink hand
Treatment Cream on forest green
Composition Hero, with the tagline

From round 1 you pointed at three things — the signature register, the on-green treatment, and the hero composition. Round 2 takes only that direction and resolves the two questions left open: does the gold record-groove icon earn its place, and does the name lead or the tagline lead. Six near-variants of one identity, not six different ideas.

The hero, resolved

Same words, same green, same hand — varying only the icon, the accent, and the hierarchy.

RECOMMENDED

R2 · Signature + Gold Groove

Icon · word · tagline

The most complete system. The gold record-groove answers the favicon/avatar gap the signature alone can’t fill — and quietly puns on “long play”. Icon above, signature, tagline beneath. This is the one that scales to every size.

Why it leads: gives you the icon extract for free, in one balanced lockup. The groove becomes your favicon and app mark.

CLEAN

R1 · Signature + Gold Rule

No icon · purest

The same hero without the record mark — just the signature, the tagline, and a short gold rule. The purest read of your pick. Cleaner, but needs a separate icon built later for small sizes.

Trade-off: most elegant, but doesn’t solve the favicon — that becomes a Step-7 job.

RESTRAINT

R3 · The Quiet Cut

Name-led · tiny tagline

Maximum restraint: the signature dominant, the tagline whisper-small beneath. The most “grown-up gallery” end — confident the name can stand nearly alone.

Read: elegant for those who already know you; least explanatory for a cold parent.

ACCENT

R4 · Gold Underline

Warmer · hand-drawn flourish

A single gold underline-flourish under the wordmark — a touch more energy and warmth. Note this cut came back slightly more brush than fine-line; closer to round-1 #03 in feel.

Watch: the flourish adds character but is one more thing to keep restrained — easy to over-sweeten.

PROVOCATION

R5 · Tagline Leads

Meaning first · name small

The open provocation made real: the tagline is the hero, the name sits small beneath with a tiny gold groove. Leads with meaning for a parent who’s never heard of you — answers the “name doesn’t say music/kids cold” worry.

Use: strong as a website hero / ad even if the logo stays name-led. A layout choice, not a logo change.

SOCIAL

R6 · The Square

1:1 · Instagram / avatar

R2’s system proven in a square — groove, signature, tagline, balanced for a social card or profile. Confirms the lockup travels from web-hero to IG without rework.

Confirms: the chosen system holds its proportions at 1:1.

Where we are

The direction is locked. Two questions left for you, then this goes to a designer to redraw vector-clean and build the full variant system.

Settled
  • Signature register — fine confident hand
  • Cream on deep forest green
  • Hero composition with the tagline
  • Fraunces + Inter for supporting type
Two calls left for you
  • Groove or no groove? R2 (with) vs R1 (without). I’d take R2 — it solves the favicon.
  • Name-led or tagline-led for the website hero? R2/R1 vs R5. Can be both: name-led logo, tagline-led hero.
  • Any cut here you’d rule out cold?
